Park Place blocks p3's Boardwalk monopoly. Handing it over lets p3 unmortgage (~$193) and build lethal dark-blue rents. Pacific does not complete green (still need NC; PA is mortgaged). Yellow set is the win condition. Never trade Park, PA, Oriental, or break yellow. No counter that includes Park Place."}}
message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to accept, reject, or counter-trade with player p3.

I have a yellow monopoly across three unmortgaged properties. The offer swaps my mortgaged Park Place for Pacific Avenue.

This trade would let p3 unmortgage Park Place and complete a dark blue monopoly with Boardwalk. Boardwalk with a hotel pays $2000 rent. Pacific Avenue is only one green property. The risk far outweighs the benefit.

Unmortgaging Park Place costs about $193. That is a steep price for a single green property. My strategy explicitly forbids trading Park Place or breaking the yellow monopoly.

p3 has $754 cash, so they can unmortgage and build immediately on the dark blue monopoly. Boardwalk with one house pays $200 and a hotel pays $2000. Pacific Avenue would give me two greens but not the full green monopoly.

A counter-offer would be futile. Pacific Avenue still leaves me without a green monopoly, and p3 needs Park Place specifically to complete dark blue. Even a large cash payment could not offset the danger of giving them that winning combination.

I can build two houses on my yellow properties for $300 and keep $57. I have no cash to mortgage. The game state shows zero houses on all three yellows, which conflicts with my earlier private notes.

I am now considering a counter-offer that keeps Park Place and demands substantial cash plus Pacific Avenue. p3 already owns two red properties and could complete the red monopoly by buying Illinois.

A counter that keeps Park Place is impossible. p3 only offered because they need it to complete dark blue. Any counter must still give up Park Place, so p3 can still build the winning monopoly. I am now calculating rent values to compare the dark blue threat against my yellow holdings.

I will reject the offer. Even a large cash payment would still leave p3 with enough money to build hotels on Boardwalk and win immediately. I am now weighing whether to waste a turn rejecting the deal in order to extract cash, or to find another property they might want without completing a winning monopoly.

I checked whether I could trade other properties to p3. Oriental Avenue would only block p1, not help p3. Pennsylvania Avenue would give them two greens but still leave them needing North Carolina. Park Place remains the only property that completes a winning monopoly. I have no tradeable assets to offer.

I will reject the trade outright. The offer frames Pacific Avenue as a helpful move toward a green monopoly, which is a trap meant to break my Park Place block. I am now drafting a public message that shuts down the deal without revealing my strategy. I am also considering a counter-offer that requests cash in exchange for an empty offer or a mortgaged property.
